sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section details the patient's admission profile, focusing on the constellation of non-specific symptoms (fever, headache, persistent hiccups) alongside classic mucocutaneous markers. It establishes the initial clinical picture, emphasizing the challenge of distinguishing between primary infection, malignancy, and inflammatory disorders before definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: Patient demographics and relevant medical history (Type 2 Diabetes)
Symptomatology: Fever, headache, arthralgia, and persistent hiccups as a sign of hyponatremia
Physical examination findings: Oral aphthae, folliculitis-like rashes, and euvolemic status
Initial laboratory anomalies: Marked hyponatremia (124 mmol/L), elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR), and rhabdomyolysis indicators
The diagnostic puzzle: Differentiating sepsis/meningitis from systemic autoimmune disease

sections.section_title: Pathophysiological Framework: Neuro-Behçet's and SIADH Mechanisms
sections.description: Before diving into the specific workup results, this section provides the essential background medicine required to understand the case. It explains the pathophysiology of Behçet's disease (BD), the rarity of concurrent neurological onset, and the mechanistic link between CNS inflammation and Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH).
subtopics: Overview of Behçet's Disease: Multisystem vasculitis and mucocutaneous hallmarks
Neuro-Behçet's Disease (Neuro-BD): Typical timing vs. rare concurrent presentation with systemic BD
Pathophysiology of SIADH in CNS inflammation: Role of cytokines (IL-6) in ADH dysregulation
Mechanisms linking severe hyponatremia to rhabdomyolysis and persistent hiccups
Why standard imaging (MRI) may appear normal in acute aseptic meningoencephalitis

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Exclusionary Workup and Confirmatory Criteria
sections.description: This section traces the logical progression from empirical treatment to definitive diagnosis. It details the step-by-step exclusion of infectious, neoplastic, and other autoimmune etiologies through CSF analysis, imaging, and serology, culminating in the application of International Criteria for Behçet's Disease.
subtopics: Exclusion of infectious causes: Negative viral/bacterial/parasitic CSF panels ruling out HSV/VZV/TB meningitis
Rule-out strategies for malignancy: Interpreting normal MRI against elevated sIL-2R levels
Differentiation from neurosarcoidosis: Normal ACE/lysozyme levels vs. inflammatory markers
**Key Turning Point:** Appearance of genital ulcers confirming systemic BD criteria (ICBD scoring)
**Final Diagnosis Synthesis:** Establishing acute Neuro-BD via aseptic meningitis findings in a BD-positive patient

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy: Conservative Management and Monotherapy Success
sections.description: This section analyzes the treatment decisions made during hospitalization. It contrasts standard guidelines (which often favor corticosteroids for Neuro-BD) with this case's successful use of colchicine monotherapy combined with conservative fluid management for SIADH.
subtopics: **Fluid Management:** Conservative management of SIADH via fluid restriction (<800 mL/day) without hypertonic saline or vaptans
**Pharmacological Pivot:** Rationale for initiating colchicine over corticosteroids or cyclophosphamide
**Colchicine Mechanism:** Anti-inflammatory effects on neutrophils and cytokine suppression (IL-1β/IL-6)
**Supportive Care:** Topical management of mucocutaneous lesions versus systemic immunosuppression needs
**Monitoring Protocols:** Tracking serum sodium normalization and resolution of neurological symptoms
